meta.tagline: An AI workflow guide for privacy, authorship, and academic judgment
meta.note: Core governance terms are defined here. Mode-specific label overrides are in the modeLabels field. UI must resolve labels through modes.json, not hard-code them.

terms.definition: A trusted, authoritative record — published scholarship, officially adopted policy, or approved institutional documentation. Safe for AI reference with proper attribution. AI output cannot return to this layer without explicit human review and validation.

Materials in active development — research in progress, draft course materials, developing policy language, or working documents not yet officially adopted. Safe for AI assistance with human review before final use.

A curated, token-budgeted extract of reviewed materials prepared specifically for AI processing. A packet contains only materials that have been routed through the governance model and confirmed as safe for external AI use. Building a packet is a deliberate governance action, not automatic.

Content generated by an AI tool — drafts, summaries, revisions, or synthesized material. AI output must be reviewed before use and cannot be re-introduced to the Canonical Source layer without explicit human validation. This is the no-recursive-upload rule.

Materials that must not enter external AI systems under any circumstances. Includes FERPA-protected student records, personnel files, confidential institutional communications, and any materials covered by institutional data governance policies. No routing decision, no exception.

Materials that have completed a review cycle and are cleared for public dissemination — conference papers, published guides, approved press materials, or official public communications. Safe after the review process is complete.

The core enforcement rule of the governance model. AI-generated output (Layer 4) cannot flow back into the Canonical Source layer (Layer 1) without explicit human review and validation. This prevents AI-generated content from silently displacing authoritative records. The packet builder enforces this as a mandatory checkpoint.

The process of assigning a material to its appropriate governance layer before deciding whether and how it can enter an AI tool. A routing decision produces a recommendation (safe, safe-with-review, or restricted) and a record that can be exported in the governance summary.

An exportable record of the routing decisions, materials processed, and review status for a single session. Suitable for institutional record-keeping, oversight committee documentation, and professional accountability. The governance summary is the primary export artifact of the tool.

Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act. Federal law protecting the privacy of student education records. Any material that contains student-identifiable information is automatically Layer 5 (Restricted) and must never enter an external AI system. This applies regardless of mode, context, or institutional policy.
